objective: Directly separate incremental floating-point error from fresh-factorization error and execute the signed downdate implementation across the admissible leverage range.
dtype_policy: Each FP32/FP64 incremental state is compared both with a fresh factorization in the same dtype and with an FP64 mathematical reference built from the exact quantized inputs supplied to the implementation.
reference_policy: The FP64 quantized reference accumulates the dtype-quantized implementation inputs exactly in FP64 and casts the accumulated state once at each fresh same-dtype checkpoint. It is a diagnostic reference, not an operational same-dtype dense accumulator.
pairing_policy: For each common seed, FP32 and FP64 use the same FP64-generated problem, update directions, and operator directions before dtype casting. Near-duplicate cumulative and random operator modes use the same metric and update trajectory; a separate RNG stream generates only the random initial operator.

signed_downdates.pairing_policy: For each rank, target leverage, operator case, and seed, form one FP64 G, M, direction, z, and random w. Cast those same tensors independently to FP32 and FP64. The requested z is calibrated to the target leverage under the original FP64 G; both the implementation-state and quantized-mathematical leverages are reported after casting.
signed_downdates.guard_policy: Run the requested admissible downdate and separately report a guard when needed. The guard scales z against the larger of (i) leverage measured by the implementation's rounded triangular state and (ii) leverage under the FP64 mathematical target represented by the quantized G. Its dtype-specific target is the representable value immediately below 0.5, with post-scale verification of both leverages. For a nonzero random operator event, w receives the same scale so both zz^T and zw^T receive the same event weight beta; for matched_z, guarded w equals guarded z; pure transport ignores w. Never substitute the guarded result for the requested result.

predeclared_correctness_criteria.backward_error_scope: Maximum over incremental_factor and incremental_operator in every positive and near-duplicate-kernel diagnostic record. Fresh-reference errors are reported but are not thresholded by this criterion; any incomplete trajectory makes the all-complete criterion false.
predeclared_correctness_criteria.guarded_error_scope: Maximum incremental_vs_fresh_same_dtype Aw relative error over every guarded signed-downdate success. A guarded failure makes the all-complete criterion false and is never omitted from the maximum/error accounting.

statistical_unit: One independently generated problem seed. Checkpoints within a trajectory are repeated measures, not independent replicates.
stopping_rule: Run every declared cell. Do not tune, filter, stop, or rerun based on confirmation outcomes.
